messages:
Jen (support): @here getting a pile of customer escalations from eu-west about streaming sessions dropping mid-response and clients doing hot reconnect loops. Reports show partial JSON chunks and then repeated 502/504 on the next open. Happening since ~06:15 UTC. :rotating_light:

Ben (oncall): On it. Can you paste a sample client log and an example request id or token? Any correlation with model or plan?

Jen (support): Here's a clipped client log (customer SDK v1.4.2):

```
[2024-11-17T06:14:07Z] sse: open 200 OK
[2024-11-17T06:14:07Z] sse: chunk id=xyz token=tok-abc size=112
[2024-11-17T06:14:08Z] sse: parse error unexpected eof
[2024-11-17T06:14:08Z] sse: connection closed by remote
[2024-11-17T06:14:09Z] sse: reconnect attempt #1
[2024-11-17T06:14:09Z] http: 504 Gateway Timeout
[2024-11-17T06:14:12Z] sse: reconnect attempt #2
```

Request id header we saw: x-rw-request-id: rw-20241117-eu-9423. Affected mostly paid plans but some free-tier seen too.

Alex (sre): Thanks. Seeing elevated 499/504 from edge in eu-west for /v1/stream endpoints. Fanout workers show incomplete frame writes then connection resets. Possible slow downstream or backpressure. I'll tail the ingress logs.

Ayden (eng): Pushing up an initial hypothesis: the lane32 fanout pool in eu-west hit a soft memory pressure and started shedding KV cache entries, which can cause chunked writes with missing trailing delimiters if the KV flush triggered mid-stream. Working on reproducer locally with long-context generate.

Marta (ops): Noted cluster autoscale in eu-west triggered a scale up around 06:13, but HPA didn't add pods fast enough and we saw queuing. I'm starting a controlled spillover to eu-central to see if client reconnect rate drops.

Ben (oncall): Steps I ran:

```
# check pods and restart suspect replicas
kubectl -n inference get pods -l region=eu-west -o wide
kubectl -n inference logs pod/fanout-22 --since=10m
kubectl -n inference exec -it pod/fanout-22 -- curl -sS localhost:8080/health
```

Fanout pod metrics show TX stalls and socket write timeouts.

incidents-bot: STATUS PAGE: Investigating — Streaming events in eu-west degraded; partial outputs and reconnect loops. See https://status.redwood.example/incident/INC-20241117-37 :eyes: \\n
Jen (support): Customers asking about refunds and data integrity — need a public note and ETA. Please confirm if we should activate fallback model routing (lower-cost small-gen) for affected tenants.

Ayden (eng): I can push an automatic fallback policy to route streaming clients to the small-gen-1 variant in eu-central for any requests hitting write timeouts > 3s. It's a config toggle, roll forward in 5m canary.

Alex (sre): Before routing changes, let's try connection-level mitigations: increase SSE keepalive heartbeat to 15s (was 10s), and increase upstream write timeout to 12s. That reduces client aggressive reconnects and gives backlog time to flush. Applying now to a couple pods to test.

Marta (ops): Applying heartbeat tweak to canary pool: done for pods fanout-22, fanout-25. Logging shows fewer premature closes. Re-routing plan queued if errors still > 5%.

Ben (oncall): Customer repro steps I documented for eng/team: (please paste into ticket)
- Start streaming generate with long prompt (>2048 tokens)
- Interrupt by simulating intermittent network (tcpdrop 200ms delay) at 3-6s window
- Observe partial JSON chunk with no trailing \"event: done\" -> client sees parse error
- Retry: client gets 504 on immediate reconnect, then succeeds after jittered backoff

Jen (support): Added that repro to all affected tickets with request id header. Also asked customers to capture client side raw bytes.

Ayden (eng): I reproduced locally with patch: when KV eviction happens concurrently with append, a race emits chunk with missing newline. Fix is to make append atomic or serialize eviction with in-flight write. Working on a 1-line guard but need a unit test.

Alex (sre): Metrics update: error rate for streaming in eu-west peaked at 6.4% around 06:16, now down to 2.1% after heartbeat tweak and canary restarts. latency p95 for first event dropped from 1.2s to 430ms after shedding some heavy tenants.

Marta (ops): Canary failover to eu-central for a sampling of tenants showed reconnect loops dropped by ~80% for those tenants. I'm preparing a staged routing update to shift 30% traffic to eu-central, 70% remain eu-west. Will monitor for 10m then increase.

incidents-bot: NOTICE: We issued a customer-facing status update at 06:42 UTC: \"Partial streaming responses and reconnect loops affecting some eu-west customers; mitigation in progress.\"

Ben (oncall): Action items:
- Ayden to ship fix for atomic append vs eviction (hotfix branch) — ETA 90m
- Marta to complete staged traffic shift and monitor — next 20m
- Alex to continue rolling heartbeat/write timeout change across pools — next 10m
- Jen to coordinate customer comms and escalation docs — ongoing

Ayden (eng): Hotfix branch created: github.com/redwood/inference/commit/48f7a2 (draft). Tests green locally. Will open PR and request expedited review.

Jen (support): Customers pinging for ETA on permanence of fix. Can we say \"short-term mitigation applied, full fix will be deployed today\" ?

Alex (sre): That's accurate based on current plan. I'll keep the incident updates rolling. Please flag any missed tenants (org IDs) to the thread.

Marta (ops): After 15m of staged spillover error rate across all eu-west traffic is down to 0.9% and reconnect incidents decreased. Holding at 30% shift for 10m to ensure stability.

incidents-bot: RESOLVED (monitoring): Partial streaming outputs and reconnect loops in eu-west reduced; mitigation in place. Full fix scheduled for today's release. Incident closed 07:28 UTC. :white_check_mark:

Jen (support): Closing tickets that reported followups. If anyone sees reappearance, re-open thread. Thanks team :thumbsup:
